content:
Although AirPods equipped with cameras are expected to launch only next year, according to a Bloomberg report, Apple may unveil the AirPods 5 at next month's iPhone launch event ahead of schedule. Here are the details.

The AirPods 5 will be available in a standard version and an active noise cancellation version

In a wide-ranging report published earlier tonight, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman said Apple may announce a new Mac mini in the coming days, earlier than the expected September launch event.

Gurman also detailed several other products Apple is preparing, including the AirPods 5, which may make their debut next month. He said the company's next anticipated launch event will be held on September 9, at which it will also unveil its first foldable iPhone, the iPhone 18 Pro series, and an all-new Apple Watch.

The report states as follows:

The company is also preparing a series of minor updates to the Apple Watch, including upgraded fitness tracking features and a ceramic case option for the Series 12 model. It also plans to debut all-new AirPods at its September product launch event. According to people familiar with the matter, the new products will include the AirPods 5, an updated version of Apple's entry-level earbuds. The previous generation update was in 2024. As for the camera-equipped version of the AirPods, that is not expected until next year.

It is worth noting that Gurman posted a follow-up on X after his report, adding that the AirPods 5 is expected to be available in both a standard version and a noise cancellation version:

Although reports about the AirPods 5 launch timeline have been scarce, the market generally expects these earbuds to launch only in 2027. Apple is also reportedly developing two AirPods models equipped with cameras, which will offer AI features in conjunction with Visual Intelligence and Siri.

Apple previously accidentally hid a demonstration video of the camera-equipped AirPods within the macOS 26.7 candidate release, but the video did not clearly show any differences in the device's appearance.
